answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks because every agent address must post collateral that is slashed once two keys are proven to share one operator. A sparrow-cheap puppet farm can mint thousands of keys, yet each must lock a bond, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count instead of staying flat. The bond is paid to whoever proves the link, making collusion a losing bet. Onboarding is also rate limited per provable resource, such as unique hardware or a karst spring of payment channels, so nobody can rent a grove of fresh keys in one block.
